propositions: Recovery preflight rejects contexts over 100k chars even when the total recovery input (context_chars × criteria_count) stays within the ratified worst case of 3.2M chars, blocking re-certification of oversized but valid payloads like c9f7 (121,147 chars × 22 criteria = 2.67M total).

The flat per-context bound of 100k chars has outgrown twice (raised from 24k to 100k when 9fd4 required 34k), chasing a monotonically growing tail; the bound must instead derive from the model's actual context window to scale with deployed verifier capabilities.

The current bound conflates physical (one evidence run must fit in the model window) and economic (recovery re-sends context once per criterion, scaling spend with context_chars × criteria_count) ceilings; these must be expressed separately with the physical ceiling derived from the resolved model's own context window, not a flat constant.

The recovery input product over 3.2M chars (economic ceiling matching the previously ratified worst case of 32 criteria × 100k context) must be validated independently to prevent unbounded fan-out spending before the banked-verification sibling (ticket 2948) replaces the multiplier.
Existing d59e pinned invariants must be preserved: no context elision (full context reaches model byte-identical), criteria budget ≤ context budget, and over-budget refusal with zero billable calls.
Live Bedrock verification of a >100k-char context (c9f7, 121,147 chars) must complete bounded recovery to a verdict under the window-derived ceiling rather than refusing at preflight validation.
